blocks.text: Canonical creature terminology: Abyssal / Abyssals. Legacy source filenames may still contain older project wording.
1. Canon authority and completion boundary
Use the locked story sequence, location names, eight mortal leaders, Hell Wardens and postgame structure as fixed narrative canon.
Use the complete 187-species dex, exact base stats/abilities, deterministic growth algorithm, validated evolution timing and species level-up learnsets as data authorities.
Trainer levels are authored and never dynamically scaled to the player.
Trainer-owned Abyssals use the same stat-growth rules as player Abyssals. There are no hidden boss IVs, secret flat stat bonuses or difficulty-only growth multipliers.
Pate and Trade receive the two starters not chosen by Aimon; Aimon never has a canonical fixed team.
Every mortal leader battle ends in surrender/defeat before the human fate decision. Human death is never inferred from team defeat.
The true level cap is 200. Ramelle deliberately looks like a conventional Level-100 endgame; Hell reveals the second half of progression.

rows:
IMPLEMENTATION PRINCIPLE
Difficulty is created by species choice, level, legal moves, held items, terrain, team ordering and AI. The engine must never secretly alter trainer stats after the battle starts.

blocks.text: Anti-loop: an AI cannot voluntarily alternate the same two Abyssals on consecutive decision cycles unless a new field/status/KO state materially changes the score.
No action-reading: the AI commits using the visible battle state before the player command is known. It may infer likely choices from revealed information, never inspect the selected command.
No unrevealed-moveset knowledge: Advanced and above may remember moves the player has already shown in that battle. They cannot query hidden player move slots.
All stochastic tie-breaking uses the battle seed so reloading does not create an exploitable different AI line without a changed game state.
4. Team construction, seeds, abilities and legal moves
4.1 Deterministic trainer individuals
1. Generic trainer growth seed key = `trainerId | teamVersion | teamSlot`. The game hashes that key using the same stable seed function used elsewhere for generated Abyssals.
2. Named characters use permanent authored seed keys and keep the same individual Abyssals across roster checkpoints unless the story explicitly records a replacement or death.
3. Higher-level trainer Abyssals simulate all historical growth rolls exactly like higher-level wild/player-generated individuals.
4. Evolution applies the normal fixed promotion delta and immediately changes future growth weights. Trainer data cannot use an under-level evolution unless the canonical evolution table allows it.
4.2 Ability assignment
Ordinary trainers: each team slot resolves permanently to Ability 1 or Ability 2 using the stable trainer-slot hash. It is never rerolled at battle start.
Elite/rare trainers: the ace uses the species Hidden Ability; all other slots use the ordinary deterministic A1/A2 rule unless explicitly stated.
Mortal leaders: ace uses Hidden Ability; additional hidden abilities appear only where listed in the leader loadout, keeping hidden abilities uncommon.
Wardens: team slots 3 and 6 use Hidden Abilities; other slots use fixed A1/A2 assignments from the authored Warden seed.
Severin: fixed ability-slot sequence HA / A2 / HA / A1 / HA / HA.
Pate’s assigned starter uses Ability 1; Trade’s assigned starter uses Ability 2. Their other ordinary checkpoint partners use authored A1/A2 seeds.
4.3 Exact legal move resolver

Trainer moves are compiled from the canonical species learnset, not rolled at runtime. This lets Checklist 12 validate legality without redesigning any trainer. Build output must materialise the final four move IDs for each trainer slot.
1. Legal pool = all level-up/evolution/relearn moves legally available to that species at or below the trainer level. No unlisted TM/tutor move is assumed.
2. Remove duplicate move IDs. Preserve normal PP exactly as defined in the move catalogue.
3. Guarantee at least one damaging STAB move when the legal pool contains one. Dual types should receive both STAB types when doing so does not destroy the trainer plan.
4. Select candidates using the trainer move profile below; tie-break by profile score, then later learn level, then lower canonical move ID. Therefore the result is deterministic.
5. Keep at least two damaging moves on ordinary trainers. CONTROL/SUSTAIN specialists may run two non-damaging moves; only authored bosses may exceed that.
6. A move that is illegal after Checklist 12 validation is replaced by the next legal candidate under the same frozen resolver; species, level and trainer identity do not change.

Advanced trainers: normally one held role on the ace from midgame onward; specialist elites may equip two. Bag heal allowance is 0–1 and is listed per record.
Mortal leaders: held slots ramp 1 / 1 / 2 / 2 / 3 / 3 / 4 / 4 from Aldren through Lucain. Bag heals ramp 1 for leaders 1–4 and 2 for leaders 5–8.
Wardens: three held-role slots each; zero external bag items. Their sustain must come from moves, abilities and terrain.
Severin: all six Abyssals equipped; two bag heals.
Cosmic Illyr/Nharos manifestations use bespoke boss mechanics and no trainer inventory.
No trainer-only held item may secretly reproduce a forbidden stat cheat. Any trainer-only item must be visible in battle data and obey its written effect.

blocks.text: 12. Severin and final-boss AI boundary
Severin Vale / King Below is a true trainer superboss: six Level-200 Abyssals, all six equipped, two bag heals, permanent authored seeds and the Severin AI tier.
Severin has no hidden stat multipliers. The challenge is the Level-200 roster, legal moves, six held items, two heals, strong switching and the best fair prediction tier.

Illyr and Nharos are not human trainers with six-Abyssal parties. They are paired cosmic boss manifestations using the Final Boss AI contract. Their effective progression spans roughly Level 188–200, with the true Level-200 climax reserved for the final phase.
Cosmic bosses cannot inspect the player’s selected command, unrevealed moves or future RNG. Dangerous effects must be telegraphed through the normal readable battle UI.

blocks.text: 13.2 Player surrender from human trainer battles
The Run command becomes Surrender / Parley in trainer battles where retreat is allowed. It is a legitimate failure state, not player death.
Key items can never be taken.

Money and eligible non-key possessions may be lost as the price of parley, including meaningful risk to equipment, unique treasure or evolution items. The exact probability/value algorithm is frozen later by Checklist 06 and Checklist 13 without reopening trainer teams.
Surrender never counts as defeating the trainer, never advances a leader fate flag, and does not grant victory XP/rewards.
13.3 Permadeath safeguards
No dynamic enemy level scaling. A player who prepares, explores and trains can become stronger than a fixed encounter.
No hidden boss stat cheating. All trainer stats can be reproduced from species, level, seed and the locked growth algorithm.
Rare/elite trainers are optional and visually/narratively signposted. They may sit up to roughly four levels above surrounding core trainers, but do not block progression.
Basic trainers do not switch proactively or use bag healing. Early route teams remain 1–3 members, limiting attrition spikes before the player has a deep reserve.
Advanced AI only switches for a clear reason; it does not endlessly cycle immunities. Leaders and Wardens use an anti-loop rule.
Except Braska’s explicit RUTHLESS identity, competent human AI will prefer a viable protective switch over knowingly spending a critically injured partner for negligible benefit.
Leader, rival and supervised battles use non-lethal final-slot protection so narrative surrender is not undermined by damage variance.
Warden fields must have at least two viable counter approaches after Checklist 05. No Warden team may cover every intended counter simultaneously.
Ordinary humans do not own mythic/box-legend tier Abyssals. High-tier species are reserved for exceptional late bosses, Wardens, Severin or explicitly authored rare encounters.
